questions.stem: Ten minutes into a unit of red blood cells, a client has chills, back pain, and a falling blood pressure. What is the first action?

options.text: Slow the transfusion and recheck in 15 minutes
Speed up to finish the unit

questions.explanation: B is correct: for any suspected reaction, stop the transfusion first. A and C keep blood running. D gives more of the blood causing the reaction.

questions.stem: Before hanging a unit of blood, how is the client matched to the unit?

options.text: One identifier, checked at the nurses' station
Two client identifiers matched at the bedside, with a second qualified checker or a barcode scan, per policy
The room number on the unit label
The client states their blood type

questions.explanation: B is correct: match two client identifiers to the unit at the bedside, with a second qualified checker or a barcode scan, per policy. A uses only one identifier, away from the bedside. C and D are not safe identifiers.

questions.stem: Which fluid may run on the same line as a blood transfusion?
questions.explanation: C is correct: use filter tubing, with only 0.9% saline on the line. A, B, and D are not the fluid the video allows.

questions.stem: How long should the nurse stay with the client after starting a transfusion?

options.text: Only until the vital signs are taken

questions.explanation: B is correct: start slowly and stay with the client for the first 15 minutes, per your policy, because the most dangerous reactions show up in the first few minutes. A is too short. C isn't a time rule. D is not what is taught.

questions.stem: Each unit of blood should be finished within what time?
questions.explanation: C is correct: finish each unit within four hours. A and B are not the limit taught. D is too long.

questions.stem: A transfusion reaction is suspected and the transfusion has been stopped. Which are next steps? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the vein open with new tubing and normal saline
Notify the provider and the blood bank
Send back the bag and tubing, plus samples, per policy
Flush the old blood tubing to keep it open
Restart the unit once the client feels better

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: new tubing and saline, stay, check vital signs, notify the provider and blood bank, and send back the bag and tubing. E pushes more blood in from the old tubing. F restarts the blood that caused the reaction.

questions.stem: During a transfusion, a client has fever, chills, flank pain, low blood pressure, and dark urine. Which reaction fits best?
questions.explanation: C is correct: acute hemolytic reactions cause fever, chills, back or flank pain, low blood pressure, and dark urine, usually from a blood type mismatch. A is fever and chills only. B is hives and itching. D raises blood pressure.

questions.stem: During a transfusion, a client develops wheezing, trouble breathing, and low blood pressure. After stopping the transfusion, what is expected?
questions.explanation: A is correct: this is anaphylaxis, so give epinephrine per protocol. B is for circulatory overload. C keeps blood running. D: hives alone and wheezing with low blood pressure are very different emergencies.

questions.stem: An older client with heart failure on a second unit has new crackles, a blood pressure of 168/94, and swollen neck veins. What is the priority?

options.text: Speed up to finish the unit
Stop it, sit the client upright, and notify
Lay the client flat with legs raised

questions.explanation: B is correct: this is likely circulatory overload, so stop, sit them up, notify, and give a diuretic per order. A adds more volume. C worsens breathing with fluid overload. D treats fever, not overload.

questions.stem: Which finding points to transfusion lung injury rather than circulatory overload?

options.text: High blood pressure and swollen neck veins
Sudden low oxygen within six hours, often with fever and low blood pressure, and no swollen neck veins

questions.explanation: B is correct: transfusion lung injury brings sudden low oxygen within six hours, often with fever and low blood pressure, and no swollen neck veins. A is circulatory overload. C is an allergic reaction. D: a diuretic won't help lung injury.
